prompts.L3:
Please expand the following bullet points into a complete, well-structured text:

- The speaker imagines becoming eight interconnected people so that life’s difficulties might disappear.
- As a single person, the speaker contains many complications within a warm, protective house roofed by an elephant’s rib cage.
- The speaker repeatedly revisits the same memories or images, though their emphasis continually shifts.
- The actors’ stable, repeated roles inspire envy, while they in turn seem to envy the speaker’s gray mornings.
- Dreams, letters, glass corridors, and stored fruit symbolize shared experiences passing among multiple selves.
prompts.L4:
Please expand the following two-sentence summary into a complete text:

The speaker confronts the burdens of a divided yet solitary identity by imagining eight interlinked selves and repeatedly rearranging dreamlike images of films, glass corridors, letters, fruit, and an elephant-ribbed house. Ultimately, multiplicity seems to dissolve difficulty, while being one contains all complications, revealing how imagination and repetition reshape—but cannot fully escape—the complexity of selfhood.
prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: i would be

outputs.L1:
I would be eight people, and then the difficulties would vanish. Only as one do I contain the complications.

In a warm house roofed with the rib cage of an elephant, I pass my grey mornings rerunning the reels. The images are the same, but the emphasis shifts. The actors bow gently to me, and I envy them their repeated parts, their constant presence in that world.

I would be eight people, each inhabiting the others’ dreams: walking through corridors of glass; framing pages; telling each other the final lines of letters; picking fruit in one dream and storing it in another.

Only as one do I contain the complications, and the images are the same—their constant presence in that world. The actors bow gently to me and envy my grey mornings.

I would be eight people beneath the rib cage of an elephant, picking fruit in a warm house above actors bowing, rerunning the reels of my presence in this world.

The difficulties vanish, and the images are the same:

eight people,  
glass corridors,  
page lines repeated,  
inhabiting grey mornings,  
roofed with my complications—

only as one,  
walking gently,  
storing my dream.
outputs.L2:
if i became eight separate selves, every hardship would dissolve; yet gathered into one, i shelter all complexity inside a heated dwelling whose ceiling is an elephant’s ribs. through ashen mornings i replay the film: nothing in the pictures changes, though each viewing draws attention elsewhere. the performers incline politely before me. i long for their endlessly recurring roles and for the permanence they possess within that realm.

i would divide into eight, every person moving through the dreams of the other seven. we would wander transparent passageways, arrange framed sheets, recite to one another the closing sentences of correspondence, harvest fruit in one sleeper’s vision and preserve it inside another’s. but as a single being, i still hold every complication. the scenes remain unchanged, as does the actors’ lasting place in that world. they offer me soft bows while coveting my colorless mornings.

i would be eight beneath the skeleton-vault of an elephant, gathering fruit in a warm home suspended over bending performers, running again the footage of my existence here. all obstacles disappear, while the pictures remain identical: eight figures, crystalline hallways, lines on pages repeating themselves, lives dwelling within dull dawns, my burdens forming the roof. only when made one do i walk tenderly onward, keeping my dream in storage.
outputs.L3:
The speaker imagines dividing into eight interconnected people, hoping that life’s difficulties might disappear if they could be shared among several selves. Yet even as a single person, the speaker already contains a complicated inner world. This complexity is enclosed within the image of a warm, protective house whose roof resembles an elephant’s rib cage—an image that suggests both shelter and confinement.

Throughout the text, the speaker repeatedly returns to the same memories, scenes, and images. Although these elements recur, their meaning is never entirely fixed; each repetition shifts the emphasis and offers a different perspective. Against this unstable inner experience, the actors appear to possess clearly defined, repeatable roles, and their apparent consistency inspires the speaker’s envy. At the same time, the actors seem to envy the speaker’s ordinary gray mornings, perhaps because those mornings represent a freedom and authenticity unavailable within scripted performance.

Images of dreams, letters, glass corridors, and stored fruit further connect the speaker’s imagined multiple selves. These symbols suggest that experiences, memories, and emotions can circulate between different identities. Together, they create a vision of the self not as a single, unified being, but as a network of related selves that share, preserve, and reinterpret the same inner life.
outputs.L4:
The speaker confronts the burden of possessing an identity that feels both divided and fundamentally alone. To explore this paradox, the speaker imagines not one stable self but eight interlinked selves, each reflecting, repeating, or transforming the others. This multiplication does not produce complete separation; instead, the eight figures remain bound together, like variations within a single consciousness. Their relationships suggest that identity can be fragmented into different roles, memories, desires, and perspectives, even though all of these parts continue to belong to one person.

Around these selves, the speaker repeatedly rearranges a series of dreamlike images: films that mediate experience, glass corridors that permit vision while creating barriers, letters that promise communication across distance, fruit associated with ripeness and bodily life, and a strange house structured like the ribs of an elephant. These images do not form a conventional narrative. They recur and shift, acquiring new meanings through repetition and altered context. The result resembles a dream, a montage, or a sequence of scenes being continually edited. Experience is not simply remembered; it is revised and reorganized by imagination.

The recurring images also express the speaker’s unstable relation to the world. Films turn life into something watched rather than directly lived. Glass corridors imply passage and connection, yet their transparent walls preserve distance and confinement. Letters attempt to carry language from one self or person to another, but they also emphasize absence. Fruit introduces color, appetite, decay, and transformation, while the elephant-ribbed house combines shelter with the monumental remains of a body. It appears protective and uncanny at once, suggesting that even the spaces in which the self seeks refuge are built from memory, mortality, and imagination.

As the sequence develops, multiplicity begins to seem strangely liberating. When identity is distributed among eight selves, burdens can be shared, contradictions can coexist, and difficult experiences can be approached from several directions. Complexity becomes manageable because no single figure must contain it all. Yet the poem’s central paradox is that being one may be more complicated than being many. A unified self must hold every memory, conflict, possibility, and loss within the same consciousness. Oneness therefore does not guarantee simplicity; it may instead contain the full pressure of multiplicity without offering any clear division of its weight.

Ultimately, the speaker’s imaginative transformations do not resolve the problem of identity. Repetition and rearrangement create movement, distance, and temporary freedom, but they cannot provide a complete escape from selfhood. The eight selves remain connected, just as the recurring images remain part of one symbolic world. Imagination can reshape experience, allowing the speaker to view it through new forms and combinations, but it cannot erase the underlying difficulty of being simultaneously divided and singular. The text thus presents identity as an ongoing act of reconstruction: the self is repeatedly broken apart and put back together, yet never reaches a final or uncomplicated form.
outputs.L5:
### I Would Be

I would be brave enough to follow my dreams, even when the path ahead seemed uncertain. I would be kind to everyone I met, because even the smallest act of compassion can change someone’s day. I would be curious, always willing to learn, explore, and see the world from a different perspective. Most importantly, I would be true to myself—not perfect, but honest, hopeful, and determined to grow.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal prose poem about fragmented identity, dreams, memory, and loneliness. Use lowercase throughout, avoid punctuation, and repeat images such as eight people, glass corridors, film reels, fruit, and a house roofed by an elephant’s rib cage.
counterfactuals.output:
i wake as eight people  
each carrying my face in a different pocket  

we walk through glass corridors  
where the night keeps its film reels  
coiled around bowls of bruised fruit  

one of us remembers a mother  
one of us remembers only rain  
one of us is still asleep  
beneath a house roofed by an elephants rib cage  

the house breathes when no one watches  
its windows fill with milk  
its doors open into glass corridors  
and the glass corridors open into me  

eight people sit at the table  
passing fruit from hand to hand  
an apple becomes a red moon  
a pear becomes a small green heart  
a plum becomes the eye of someone  
who once knew my name  

in the cellar the film reels turn  
showing memories i never lived  
a birthday without candles  
a river flowing through a bed  
eight people waving from the opposite shore  

i call to them  
but my voice is locked inside the fruit  

morning arrives wearing my clothes  
it finds the house roofed by an elephants rib cage  
empty except for the slow machinery of dreams  

the glass corridors lengthen  
the film reels burn without light  
eight people become seven  
then six  
then one  
then eight again  

i search each face for the missing room  
where loneliness sleeps on a white chair  
holding a bowl of fruit  
and listening to the elephant bones  
remember the body they once protected  

perhaps i am the house  
perhaps i am the roof  
perhaps i am only the space between the ribs  

still the eight people enter me  
still the glass corridors divide me  
still the film reels whisper my unfinished lives  

and far inside the dream  
beneath the fruit beneath the memory  
someone wakes alone  
with eight shadows  
and no name
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an experimental stream-of-consciousness poem in which the speaker wishes to become eight interconnected people but remains trapped as one. Let phrases and images recur with shifting emphasis, like footage being replayed.
counterfactuals.output:
I want to become eight people  
holding hands inside one weather—

eight windows lit in a building  
with only one room.

I would be the one who wakes,  
the one who keeps sleeping,  
the one at the sink rinsing a red cup,  
the one already leaving,  
the one who says stay,  
the one who hears it too late,  
the one behind the camera,  
the one crossing the frame again—

crossing the frame again,  
coat open, mouth full of snow.

But the footage stutters.

There I am at the sink.  
There I am at the sink.  
There I—

one hand, one red cup,  
seven reflections hovering  
in the dark kitchen glass.

If I could divide cleanly  
we would share a nervous system of streets:  
you touch a railing in the north  
and I shiver in the south;  
someone laughs underground  
and all our teeth flash;  
someone loses a name  
and eight mouths go looking.

Eight mouths go looking  
through the same sentence.

The sentence is a hallway.  
The hallway is the building.  
The building has eight windows lit  
and only one room.

Rewind:

the one who wakes turns off the alarm.  
The one who sleeps dreams the alarm is rain.  
The one at the sink drops the red cup.  
The one already leaving stops.  
The one who says stay says nothing.  
The one who hears it turns.  
The one behind the camera enters the frame.  
The one crossing the frame—

crosses the frame—

crosses—

No. Again.

I want to become eight people  
not copies, not mirrors,  
but knots in a single bright net,  
each tug traveling,  
each wound distributed  
until pain is only weather.

Instead I am one nail  
trying to be a constellation.

Instead I carry seven empty coats  
through the station.  
Their sleeves take turns touching me.  
Their pockets contain  
the same ticket, the same key,  
the same small red shard of cup.

Playback:

snow enters my mouth.  
The mouth becomes a window.  
The window becomes a hand  
holding another hand  
holding another—

until the chain arrives  
at the first hand,

my hand,

alone at the sink  
in the building  
in the weather,

washing the unbroken cup,

washing the broken cup,

washing eight cups with one hand  
while seven shadows whisper  
from the dark glass:

again,  
again,  
again—

and I remain  
the footage and the frame,  
the departure and the stay,

eight windows blazing,

one room  
that will not open.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a dreamlike prose poem inspired by surrealism and cut-up techniques, using motifs of actors, grey mornings, letters, glass corridors, shared dreams, and an elephant skeleton. Make the ending increasingly fragmented.
counterfactuals.output:
At nine o’clock the actors removed their faces  
and hung them from the fire escape.  
A grey morning entered without applause,  
carrying a tray of unopened letters—  
each envelope addressed to a different silence.

We rehearsed the weather in a glass corridor.  
You played the window; I played the stone  
thrown gently through you. Beyond the walls,  
an elephant skeleton wandered the city,  
its ivory rooms full of blue moths,  
its ribs chiming whenever someone lied.

No one remembered who had written the script.  
Pages arrived in the wrong order:

**THE MOON:** I have misplaced my childhood.  
**THE DOOR:** There is no childhood, only hinges.  
**THE ACTORS:** Then whose footprints are these?

Grey morning after grey morning,  
we mailed ourselves to imaginary countries.  
The letters came back damp with sleep.  
Inside them, our shared dream kept changing clothes:  
first a station, then a flooded theatre,  
then the long glass corridor  
where the elephant skeleton bent down  
and whispered through its empty cathedral—

You are awake in the wrong person.

After that, language began losing its buttons.  
The actors spoke in feathers.  
The letters opened us.

Glass  
corridor  
grey mouth morning—

someone exits carrying my name  
someone enters without bones

elephant / envelope / elegy

we dreamed  
we shared  
we—

the ribs ring  
the stage snows upward  
your face in the wall in the letter in

no curtain only  
only

grey  
g—  
     l—  
          ass

and the enormous white animal  
un  
     walking  
          us
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a single-paragraph literary monologue about multiplicity versus solitude. Include the repeated lines “i would be eight people,” “only as one i contain the complications,” and “the images are the same,” while rearranging surrounding language into strange new combinations.
counterfactuals.output: “i would be eight people,” I tell the mirror, and the mirror opens its silver mouths: one to remember, one to flee, one to sleep beneath the staircase of noon, one to wear my name backward, one to forgive the locked garden, one to count the blue machinery of sorrow, one to laugh with a stranger’s teeth, and one to remain alone; yet “only as one i contain the complications,” only in this narrow vessel where every voice collides like weather in a drawer, where tenderness grows elbows and fear combs its bright feathers; “the images are the same,” whether I divide or gather, the same house drinking rain, the same moon folded into a pocket, the same hand waving from the bottom of the hour; “i would be eight people,” I insist, because solitude is a room that multiplies its doors, because company is sometimes merely loneliness wearing many coats, but “only as one i contain the complications,” the knots of honey, the bruised arithmetic, the little republics arguing behind my eyes; “the images are the same,” says the mirror, says the rain, says each abandoned version of me, and I stand among them singular and crowded, a choir trapped inside one note.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an unpunctuated lowercase poem that feels like a damaged film loop: begin with a desire to be eight people, move through a warm house and overlapping dreams, then collage earlier phrases into a disorienting final passage.
counterfactuals.output:
i want to be eight people

one to enter the warm house
one to leave the door breathing
one to sleep beneath the table
one to keep the windows dreaming
one to wear the smoke like hair
one to remember the fire
one to wake inside your dream
one to watch me disappear

the house is warm with yellow rooms
the walls lean close to hear us
your dream crosses through my dream
two rivers under one sheet
we meet where the water flickers
we speak with the same lost mouth

then the film catches

i want the warm door
to be eight windows
sleeping beneath your yellow dream
the house wears my hair
the river remembers the table
one room enters another room
one mouth leaves the fire breathing

your dream your dream the walls flicker
eight people under one sheet
i disappear into the warm
i disappear into the house
the house crosses through my smoke
the smoke wakes inside the water

then the film catches

one to enter
one to enter
one to enter the lost mouth
eight rivers wearing windows
yellow hair beneath the fire
your house dreaming my house
my dream leaving your dream

i want i want i want
the warm people
the breathing table
the door beneath the river
the one who watches
the eight who disappear
the house the house the house
still flickering inside us
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
